prompt_quality_framework.heading: Better Context. Better Questions. Better Review.

principles.name: Task
principles.description: State precisely what Copilot should do (draft, summarize, analyze, extract, or explain).

principles.name: Context
principles.description: Explain why the task is being performed and provide background business circumstances.

principles.name: Source
principles.description: Reference authorized files, notes, or data rows that must serve as the sole factual basis.

principles.name: Audience
principles.description: Define who will read or use the output (executives, clients, operations staff, or team members).

principles.name: Constraints
principles.description: Set negative boundaries (no invented facts, specific length limits, excluded topics, or confidentiality rules).

principles.name: Format
principles.description: Specify output structure (bulleted list, executive memo, tabular layout, or presentation outline).

principles.name: Verification
principles.description: Instruct Copilot to flag assumptions, cite sources, or mark items requiring human confirmation.

examples.word: Using the supplied fictional operations notes, draft a one-page management summary. Include only supported findings. Do not invent figures, customer names or decisions. Mark missing information as needing confirmation.
examples.excel: Analyze the provided sales data by month and category. Explain the formulas and list the source columns used. Do not invent data. Highlight assumptions, then provide calculations I can verify manually.
examples.powerpoint: Create a proposed presentation outline from the approved report. Preserve all dates and figures exactly, avoid unsupported claims, and identify content that requires visual or factual review.
examples.meeting: Summarize the supplied fictional transcript. Extract only decisions and action items explicitly stated. Do not invent owners or deadlines. Mark unclear ownership as unconfirmed.

prompt_quality_framework.teaching_point: A more detailed prompt can improve outputs, but it cannot guarantee accuracy. Human verification remains mandatory.

microsoft_graph_work_iq_policy.heading: Copilot Can Use Authorized Work Context—not Every File in the Organization.
principles: Copilot respects organizational permissions and only accesses information the authenticated user has explicit permission to view.

Oversharing Risk Awareness: If internal folders or SharePoint sites have overly broad permissions, Copilot can surface sensitive content unintentionally. Students are taught to audit document permissions.
Least Privilege Standard: Always restrict working files to necessary collaborators before referencing them in AI prompts.
Synthetic Classroom Scenarios: All exercises use isolated synthetic datasets representing public business policy, team project reports, and fictional restricted documents.

ai_output_verification_standard.heading: Never Approve an AI Result You Cannot Explain or Check.
ai_output_verification_standard.workflow: Generate → Inspect → Compare → Recalculate → Correct → Approve

verification_types.scope: Verify all names, dates, quotes, references, and operational business details against original notes.
Perform 100% independent manual recalculation of totals, percentages, formula ranges, and trend calculations.
Audit source alignment, eliminate omitted caveats, and remove fabricated or hallucinated citations.
Check recipient lists, subject lines, tone appropriateness, commitments made, and action item ownership.
Inspect slide legibility, chart scales, axis labels, and ensure graphics do not mislead the audience.
Confirm that source data was authorized for use, adheres to privacy rules, and has documented human sign-off.

common_errors_caught: Wrong formula syntax and incorrect Excel ranges
Invented meeting commitments and misassigned owners
Omitted safety caveats and financial assumptions

teams_meeting_intelligence_policy.heading: Meeting Intelligence & Consent Governance
principles: Live During-Meeting Copilot can assist with questions in real time without requiring persistent transcripts when enabled by organizers.
Post-Meeting Recaps and action-item tracking strictly require meeting recording or transcription.
Zero Unauthorized Recording: No learner is ever required or permitted to record real workplace meetings without explicit attendee consent. Classroom labs utilize fictional transcripts.

excel_ai_reliability_policy.heading: Use AI to Assist Analysis. Keep the Calculations Verifiable.
mandatory_checks: Confirm source dataset is structured with clear headers and no merged header cells.
Verify that Copilot correctly identified the intended target columns.
Audit formula logic: ensure range bounds and criteria match the business question.
Validate date parsing and period groupings.
Recalculate key totals and category summaries manually.
Reconcile chart values directly against raw spreadsheet tables.
Confirm that analytical conclusions are supported by actual numerical evidence.
Disclose analytical limitations and assumptions in executive summaries.
excel_ai_reliability_policy.scope_boundary: Focuses on everyday spreadsheet reporting and formula verification; excludes advanced Power Query, complex DAX, Power BI, and Python in Excel.

responsible_ai_policy.heading: Responsible AI, Privacy & Workplace Data Safety
core_rules: Human Accountability: The user, not the AI, bears full professional responsibility for all approved documents, numbers, and communications.
Confidential Data Protection: Never enter sensitive personal identifiable information (PII), confidential client contracts, or trade secrets into public AI tools.
Prompt Injection Defense: Inspect external or unvetted source documents for hidden malicious instructions before feeding them to Copilot.
Transparent AI Disclosure: Document where AI assistance was utilized and maintain a human verification audit trail.

faqs.q: What is Microsoft 365 Copilot — AI Workplace Productivity?
faqs.a: It is a practical 4-week, 32-hour applied specialization covering AI-assisted workplace tasks across Microsoft Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook, and Teams, with a strong, non-negotiable emphasis on factual verification, prompt engineering, and responsible business data governance.

faqs.q: What is the course duration and total learning hours?
faqs.a: The course spans exactly 4 weeks with 32 structured learning hours across 6 comprehensive modules (4h + 6h + 6h + 6h + 6h + 4h = 32 hours), requiring approximately 8 hours of dedicated weekly learning.

faqs.q: What is the course fee?
faqs.a: The course fee is a flat, transparent ₹5,900 with zero hidden charges, artificial discounts, or deceptive compare-at pricing. This fee covers all instruction, course materials, guided simulations, and certification assessment.

faqs.q: Who should take this course?
faqs.a: Existing Microsoft 365 users, office administrators, executives, department managers, business analysts, educators, consultants, and small business owners who want to adopt AI-assisted productivity tools while maintaining complete accountability for final workplace outputs.

faqs.q: Is this course suitable for complete computer beginners?
faqs.a: No. This is an applied AI workplace upskilling program that requires basic proficiency in Microsoft Word, Excel, and PowerPoint (document formatting, simple formulas, basic slide creation). Complete beginners lacking core office fundamentals should first complete Course 30 — Office Productivity Professional.

faqs.q: What is Microsoft 365 Copilot?
faqs.a: Microsoft 365 Copilot is Microsoft's enterprise AI workplace experience that combines advanced Large Language Models (LLMs) with authorized organizational context via Microsoft Graph and Work IQ, integrated directly into Microsoft 365 desktop and web applications.

faqs.q: What is Microsoft Copilot Chat?
faqs.a: Microsoft Copilot Chat is a conversational AI interface available to eligible Microsoft 365 work and school accounts that offers web-grounded search, document drafting, text summarization, and file interaction with commercial data protection.

faqs.q: Is Copilot Chat the same as full licensed Microsoft 365 Copilot?
faqs.a: No. While Copilot Chat provides valuable conversational AI assistance, full Microsoft 365 Copilot requires an eligible paid add-on license that unlocks deep Microsoft Graph work-data grounding, in-app canvas sidebars across Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and Outlook, and advanced Teams meeting recaps.

faqs.q: Does every Microsoft 365 subscription include full Copilot?
faqs.a: No. Full Copilot features require specific eligible base licenses (such as Microsoft 365 Business Standard/Premium or E3/E5) plus an active Microsoft 365 Copilot add-on subscription, subject to organizational tenant enablement.

faqs.q: Will I learn how to use Copilot in Microsoft Word?
faqs.a: Yes. You will learn to draft executive reports, proposals, and briefs from notes, summarize lengthy documents, adapt tone and writing style, and systematically verify AI drafts against source materials.

faqs.q: Will I learn how to use Copilot in Microsoft Excel?
faqs.a: Yes. You will learn structured data preparation, AI formula suggestions, spreadsheet insights, automated data summaries, and chart suggestions, combined with mandatory manual recalculation techniques.

faqs.q: Can Copilot make spreadsheet and calculation mistakes?
faqs.a: Yes. Microsoft explicitly documents that AI-generated spreadsheet formulas and insights can misread ranges, hallucinate figures, or apply flawed calculation logic. The course teaches strict independent formula auditing so you never approve unverified numbers.

faqs.q: Will I learn how to use Copilot in Microsoft PowerPoint?
faqs.a: Yes. You will learn to convert Word source reports and outlines into draft slide decks, evaluate AI design suggestions, refine layouts, and audit visual claims for accuracy and consistency.

faqs.q: Does Copilot create finished, perfect presentations automatically?
faqs.a: No. Copilot generates a helpful starting outline and draft slides, but human design refinement, brand alignment, visual hierarchy adjustment, and factual data checking remain strictly necessary.

faqs.q: Will I learn how to use Copilot in Microsoft Outlook?
faqs.a: Yes. You will practice summarizing complex email threads, drafting professional replies with calibrated tone, extracting follow-up tasks, and using Copilot's coaching features to refine communications.

faqs.q: Will I learn how to use Copilot in Microsoft Teams?
faqs.a: Yes. You will learn to navigate meeting recaps, extract stated decisions and action items, verify task ownership, and draft professional post-meeting stakeholder summaries.

faqs.q: Can Teams Copilot work in meetings without transcription?
faqs.a: Yes, certain live during-meeting Copilot questions can function without recording or transcription if enabled by the meeting organizer. However, post-meeting summaries, recaps, and action-item tracking require meeting transcription or recording.

faqs.q: Can Copilot access all confidential company files across an organization?
faqs.a: No. Copilot strictly respects existing user permissions configured in Microsoft 365 and Microsoft Graph. It only accesses content that the signed-in user already has explicit permission to read, though users must be vigilant regarding organizational oversharing.

faqs.q: What is Microsoft Graph and Work IQ grounding?

faqs.q: Is Copilot Studio or custom AI agent development included in this course?

faqs.q: Is Azure AI development part of this course?

faqs.q: Do I need to buy a paid Microsoft Copilot license to take this course?

faqs.q: Does the course fee include a Microsoft 365 Copilot subscription?

faqs.q: Will I practice with real company confidential data?

faq.q: What is the course duration and total learning hours?
faq.a: The course spans exactly 4 weeks with 32 structured learning hours across 6 comprehensive modules (4h + 6h + 6h + 6h + 6h + 4h = 32 hours), requiring approximately 8 hours of dedicated weekly learning.

faq.q: What is the course fee?
faq.a: The course fee is a flat, transparent ₹5,900 with zero hidden charges, artificial discounts, or deceptive compare-at pricing. This fee covers all instruction, course materials, guided simulations, and certification assessment.

faq.q: Who should take this course?
faq.a: Existing Microsoft 365 users, office administrators, executives, department managers, business analysts, educators, consultants, and small business owners who want to adopt AI-assisted productivity tools while maintaining complete accountability for final workplace outputs.

faq.q: Is Copilot Chat the same as full licensed Microsoft 365 Copilot?

faq.q: Will I learn how to use Copilot in Microsoft Word?
faq.a: Yes. You will learn to draft executive reports, proposals, and briefs from notes, summarize lengthy documents, adapt tone and writing style, and systematically verify AI drafts against source materials.

faq.q: Will I learn how to use Copilot in Microsoft Excel?

faq.q: Can Copilot make spreadsheet and calculation mistakes?
faq.a: Yes. Microsoft explicitly documents that AI-generated spreadsheet formulas and insights can misread ranges, hallucinate figures, or apply flawed calculation logic. The course teaches strict independent formula auditing so you never approve unverified numbers.

faq.q: Does Copilot create finished, perfect presentations automatically?

faq.q: Will I learn how to use Copilot in Microsoft Outlook?

faq.q: Will I learn how to use Copilot in Microsoft Teams?

faq.a: Yes, certain live during-meeting Copilot questions can function without recording or transcription if enabled by the meeting organizer. However, post-meeting summaries, recaps, and action-item tracking require meeting transcription or recording.
